deviation_mechanism: In the first optimization pass, the solver operates with unconstrained or broad initialization bounds. Multi-layer interference conditions (phase matching, edge roll-off steepness) often temporarily favor optical thicknesses well above the nominal quarter-wave value (λ/4n) to exploit higher-order constructive interference or compensate for material dispersion gradients. Without explicit geometric bounds, the gradient-based or stochastic search explores these wider parameter volumes before the objective landscape funnels solutions back into the efficient thin-film regime. The excursions past 150 nm are therefore a natural artifact of early-stage exploratory optimization rather than a fundamental flaw in the target physics.
